discrete_risks.name: Sustained human-to-human transmission of an H5 influenza virus
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: WHO or a national health authority publicly confirms an H5 (any neuraminidase) influenza cluster with at least three sequential generations of human-to-human transmission, or a cluster of at least 10 epidemiologically linked human cases with no plausible animal or environmental exposure for the majority.
discrete_risks.reasoning: The B3.13 dairy-cattle reservoir plus D1.1/D1.2 spillovers into cattle and swine give H5 unprecedented mammalian passage opportunity, and swine co-infection is the classic reassortment route. But the empirical signal in 2026 is deceleration in humans, not acceleration: only 12 confirmed global H5N1 human cases Aug 2025-Jun 2026, and the first-ever H5N5 human case (Washington, Nov 2025) produced zero secondary transmission. Adaptive mutations keep appearing sporadically without fixing. CDC IRAT holds recent isolates at moderate.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: Zero sustained H5 human transmission in 29 years since 1997 (Hong Kong), across ~1,022 human cases and repeated family clusters (the 2006 Karo, Indonesia cluster of 8 was closest and still died out). Reference class of any novel influenza A subtype achieving sustained human spread: 4 events (1918, 1957, 1968, 2009) in ~108 years, about 3.7%/yr for all subtypes combined; H5 is one candidate among several (H7, H9, H3N8, swine H1/H3).
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: Two directions. Upward: US surveillance capacity has fallen sharply (CDC workforce down a third, state health department attrition), so 'no detected transmission' increasingly means 'not looking', and the true probability may be materially higher. Downward: H5 has had two decades of intense mammalian exposure - fur farms, marine mammals, cats, cattle - without adapting, which is evidence the barrier is genuinely hard rather than that we have been lucky. Forecasters who over-updated on the 2024 dairy story have been punished for two consecutive years.

discrete_risks.name: WHO declares an influenza pandemic (any subtype)
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: WHO formally declares an influenza pandemic, or declares a PHEIC/pandemic emergency for a novel influenza A virus with confirmed sustained community-level human-to-human transmission in at least two WHO regions.
discrete_risks.reasoning: Broader than H5: includes swine-origin H1/H3 variants (the 2009 route), H7N9 re-emergence, H9N2, and reassortants. The ongoing global panzootic raises the reassortment substrate, while post-2020 mRNA and cell-based platform capacity does not reduce emergence probability at all - only response speed, which has itself been degraded by BARDA's cancellation of 22 mRNA programmes.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: 4 recognized influenza pandemics in 108 years (1918, 1957, 1968, 2009), plus the 1977 re-emergence: roughly 3.7-4.6% per year. Poisson with lambda 0.04/yr gives 5.5% by end-2027, 19% by end-2031, 33% by end-2036 - I am adopting essentially the base rate with a small upward nudge.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: WHO declaration behavior has changed post-2009 and post-COVID: after the 2009 overreaction criticism and the 2024 IHR amendments creating a 'pandemic emergency' tier, the Secretariat may declare faster and more often for milder events, inflating this probability without corresponding real-world severity. Conversely, US rejection of the IHR amendments plus WHO's fiscal weakness could make the DG more reluctant to declare against major-power objection.

discrete_risks.name: A newly emerged pathogen causes at least 1 million cumulative deaths worldwide
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: A pathogen not endemically circulating in humans as of 1 Jan 2026 is credibly estimated by WHO, IHME, or a peer-reviewed consensus source to have caused at least 1,000,000 cumulative human deaths (reported or excess) within the stated horizon.
discrete_risks.reasoning: Strictly harder than 'a pandemic is declared' - 2009 H1N1 killed roughly 150k-580k and would not qualify. Requires both emergence and high severity or high attack rate. Modern ICU capacity, antivirals and rapid vaccine platforms cut CFR relative to 1918; global connectivity and 8.2 billion people cut the other way. Degraded WHO financing and US surveillance modestly slow containment.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: Emergent pathogens killing at least 1M cumulatively since 1900: 1918 flu, 1957 flu, 1968 flu, HIV, COVID-19 = 5 events in 108 years, about 4.6%/yr, but three cluster in the influenza-naive early/mid century. Post-1970 rate: HIV and COVID = 2 in 56 years, about 3.6%/yr. I use roughly 2.5%/yr reflecting improved countermeasures.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: The COVID experience may have durably raised both baseline population immunity to sarbecoviruses and the speed of countermeasure deployment, meaning the next emergence is caught at a lower level - pushing this well below base rate. In the other direction, my estimate could be far too low if AI-enabled design collapses the barrier to constructing a high-severity agent, which would decouple the future rate entirely from the natural-emergence base rate that dominates my anchor.

discrete_risks.name: WHO declares at least one new PHEIC beyond polio and the current Ebola BDBV emergency
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: WHO's Director-General determines a new Public Health Emergency of International Concern (or pandemic emergency under the amended IHR) for an event distinct from the standing polio PHEIC and the Ebola Bundibugyo PHEIC declared 17 May 2026, at any point in the window.
discrete_risks.reasoning: Purely a rate question. WHO has become progressively more willing to use the instrument, and the amended IHR (in force 19 Sept 2025) added a pandemic emergency tier that if anything increases declaration frequency. Live candidates: mpox clade Ib re-escalation (including the recombinant Ib/IIb virus flagged in DON 2026-DON595 and the Sindh neonatal cluster), Marburg, Nipah, a novel influenza, cholera, or an arbovirus such as Oropouche.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: PHEICs declared 2009-2026: H1N1 (2009), polio (2014), Ebola West Africa (2014), Zika (2016), Ebola Kivu (2019), COVID-19 (2020), mpox (2022), mpox (2024), Ebola BDBV (2026) = 9 in 17 years, about 0.53/yr. Poisson gives 53% by end-2027 and 94% by end-2031.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: A PHEIC is an administrative act, not an epidemiological fact. A financially crippled WHO facing US hostility may become more conservative to avoid triggering trade and travel retaliation against member states - the DG explicitly declined to declare for several 2023-25 events. Also, if the Ebola PHEIC drags on, WHO may fold new events into existing determinations rather than declare fresh ones, resolving this NO on a technicality.

discrete_risks.name: Current DRC/Uganda Bundibugyo Ebola epidemic exceeds 10,000 confirmed cases
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: WHO/AFRO situation reports for the outbreak declared 15 May 2026 (or its recognized continuation) record at least 10,000 cumulative laboratory-confirmed cases across all affected countries.
discrete_risks.reasoning: At 3,262 confirmed cases 10 weeks in and adding roughly 900/week with acceleration, linear extrapolation reaches 10,000 by about October 2026. The critical structural fact is the absence of a licensed BDBV vaccine or monoclonal - ring vaccination is what capped Kivu 2018-20 at 3,470 cases over 23 months. Add Ituri/North Kivu armed-group insecurity, a 60%-unfunded WHO appeal, degraded US surveillance support, and suspected-case declines that experts read as testing collapse rather than control.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: Ebola outbreaks exceeding 10,000 confirmed-plus-probable cases: 1 of roughly 35 recorded outbreaks since 1976 (West Africa 2014-16, ~28,600). Conditional on an outbreak already exceeding 3,000 confirmed cases: 1 of 2 (West Africa yes, Kivu no) - but Kivu had a vaccine and this does not.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: Every large Ebola outbreak has been over-extrapolated at the exponential stage - the September 2014 CDC projection of 1.4 million cases by January 2015 overshot by roughly 50x, because behavioral change (safe burials, avoidance of health facilities, community mobilization) is a powerful nonlinear brake independent of vaccines. Bundibugyo has historically lower transmissibility and CFR (~34% in 2007-08) than Zaire ebolavirus. The current 44% CFR likely reflects under-ascertainment of mild cases, which cuts both ways on projected counts.

discrete_risks.name: Ebola causes a confirmed secondary transmission chain outside Africa
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: A national health authority in a country outside the WHO African Region confirms at least one locally acquired Ebola (any species) infection in a person who was not infected in Africa, at any point in the window.
discrete_risks.reasoning: Already exported: one case in France, a US aid worker medevaced to Germany 13 July 2026, and two DRC-diagnosed patients treated in Germany. Bundibugyo has no licensed post-exposure monoclonal or vaccine, so occupational protection for healthcare workers depends entirely on PPE discipline. The larger and longer the DRC epidemic, the more exportation draws.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: Secondary transmission outside Africa across all Ebola history: 2 events (Dallas 2014, 2 nurses; Madrid 2014, 1 nurse), both during the ~28,600-case West Africa epidemic. Zero secondary cases outside Africa from the Kivu, Sudan-Uganda 2022, or 2025 outbreaks despite multiple medevacs.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: Post-2014, high-income countries built dedicated biocontainment units and rehearsed protocols; every subsequent medevac has been handled without onward transmission, which is 10+ years of clean evidence that this is now well managed, so 12% may be roughly 2x too high. The counter-counter: undiagnosed travelers presenting to ordinary emergency departments, not medevacs, are the real risk pathway, and that pathway scales with epidemic size.

discrete_risks.name: United States formally loses measles elimination status
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: PAHO's Regional Verification Commission (or WHO) formally announces that the United States no longer meets measles elimination criteria, or the US government/CDC publicly acknowledges loss of elimination status.
discrete_risks.reasoning: The technical case is already made: whole-genome sequencing shows the D8-9171 lineage in continuous domestic circulation since the January 2025 West Texas outbreak, well past the 12-month threshold, and outside experts declared elimination over in practice on 24 June 2026. The RVC reviews in November 2026. Residual uncertainty is procedural and political, not epidemiological.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: Countries in the Americas that lost measles elimination after achieving it: Venezuela (2018) and Brazil (2019) - 2 of roughly 35 in the region since 2016, both after 12+ months of confirmed endemic lineage transmission. Conditional on documented >12-month single-lineage transmission plus formal RVC review, the historical resolution rate is near 100%; I discount for US-specific political friction and possible deferral.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: The RVC could defer rather than revoke, citing incomplete US surveillance data - and with CDC's workforce down a third and the administration hostile to the framing, the US may simply decline to submit the documentation that would trigger revocation, leaving the status formally unresolved for years. 'Everyone agrees it is gone but nobody declares it' is a genuinely plausible outcome and would resolve this NO.

discrete_risks.name: US reports at least 5,000 confirmed measles cases in a single calendar year
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: CDC's official measles surveillance reports at least 5,000 confirmed cases for any single calendar year within the window.
discrete_risks.reasoning: 2025 finished around 2,200 and 2026 stood at 2,295 on 22 July with the seasonal peak (Feb-May) past, implying roughly 2,800-3,300 for the full year - growth but not explosive. Reaching 5,000 requires either a large outbreak in a dense undervaccinated metro (NYC-style) or continued coverage erosion. Kindergarten MMR at 92.5% with 3.6% exemptions is meaningfully below the 95% threshold and falling roughly 0.3-0.5pp/yr, so susceptible cohorts accumulate mechanically.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: US annual measles counts since elimination in 2000: 2014 (667), 2019 (1,274), 2025 (~2,200), 2026 (~2,300 YTD). The last year above 5,000 was 1990 (27,786) during the pre-VFC epidemic. Successive record years have roughly doubled every 5-6 years; 5,000 is about one more doubling.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: Measles outbreaks are extremely spatially clumped in specific tight-knit communities, and once a community is burned through (as West Texas largely was) it cannot supply a second wave for a decade. The 2025-26 numbers may represent one-off depletion rather than a new baseline, and counts could fall back to the low hundreds by 2028 even with declining coverage. National coverage is a poor predictor - pockets matter, and pocket formation is slow.

discrete_risks.name: US federal government de-recommends a core routine childhood vaccine and the change survives
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: CDC's published child and adolescent immunization schedule removes a currently universally-recommended antigen (MMR, DTaP, IPV, Hib, PCV, rotavirus, varicella, or the hepatitis B birth dose) from universal recommendation - moving it to shared clinical decision-making, risk-based, or off-schedule - and that change is in effect and not judicially stayed for at least 6 continuous months.
discrete_risks.reasoning: This has already been attempted: ACIP moved the hepatitis B birth dose to shared clinical decision-making and split MMRV under age 4, and HHS announced a January 2026 schedule overhaul outside the ACIP process covering hepatitis A, rotavirus and influenza. The only thing preventing resolution today is the D. Mass. stay of 16 March 2026, which reverted the schedule to January 2025 versions. The question is whether the administration wins on the merits or reissues in a procedurally durable form before January 2029.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: No reference class exists - no US administration has de-recommended a core childhood antigen since ACIP's founding in 1964 (RotaShield's 1999 withdrawal was for a genuine intussusception safety signal, a different mechanism). This forecast is almost entirely inside-view: a sitting HHS Secretary with an explicit agenda, a reconstituted ACIP, and roughly 30 months of remaining term.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: Courts have blocked the administration twice already; AAP and the state alliances publish competing schedules that insurers and the Vaccines for Children programme are largely following; and the ACA preventive-services mandate plus state law create redundant legal anchors. The federal schedule may become a nullity rather than a lever - de-recommendation on paper that never takes practical effect and gets enjoined within 6 months, resolving this NO repeatedly. There is also real probability the Secretary departs before 2029.

discrete_risks.name: PABS annex to the WHO Pandemic Agreement adopted by a World Health Assembly
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: A World Health Assembly (regular or special session) formally adopts the Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing annex to the WHO Pandemic Agreement.
discrete_risks.reasoning: IGWG has missed its WHA79 (May 2026) deadline and extended twice (28 March and 1 May 2026); IGWG7 concluded in July 2026 without agreement and IGWG8 runs 14-18 September 2026, with WHA80 in May 2027 as the stated target. The core dispute - the 20% real-time production set-aside, genetic sequence data scope, and intellectual property - is a genuine North-South distributional fight, not a drafting problem. A June 2026 open letter to G7/G20/BRICS leaders signals the negotiation needs political rescue.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: Multilateral health instrument annex/protocol negotiations: the FCTC Illicit Trade Protocol took 5 years of INB after the treaty (2007-2012); the Nagoya Protocol took 6 years after the CBD ABS mandate. Two extensions already consumed suggests modal completion in 2027-2029, not 2026.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: Deadline-driven multilateral processes usually do close once a hard political deadline is set, and WHA80 coincides with a DG transition that creates strong legacy incentives to deliver. Equally plausible in the other direction: with the US outside WHO and unable to be bound, pharmaceutical-hosting countries (EU, Switzerland, Japan, UK) have less reason to accept binding obligations their largest competitor escapes, which could stall this indefinitely rather than for two more years.

discrete_risks.name: WHO Pandemic Agreement enters into force
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: The 60th instrument of ratification, acceptance, approval or accession to the WHO Pandemic Agreement is deposited, bringing the Agreement into force.
discrete_risks.reasoning: Sequential dependency: the Agreement only opens for signature after the PABS annex is adopted, then requires 60 ratifications. Even on an optimistic path (annex May 2027, signature opens mid-2027), national ratification in 60 countries typically takes 2-5 years. Entry into force before 2029 is close to impossible; 2029-2031 is the realistic central case, conditional on the annex landing.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: WHO FCTC: adopted May 2003, opened for signature June 2003, 40th ratification November 2004, in force February 2005 - 21 months, but with a lower threshold and far broader consensus. Nagoya Protocol: adopted 2010, 50th ratification 2014, in force October 2014 - 4 years. The Pandemic Agreement needs 60 and faces active opposition; 3-5 years post-signature is the fair anchor.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: Ratification could be far faster than base rate because roughly 120 countries already voted to adopt and low- and middle-income countries have a direct material interest in the 20% allocation - they may ratify quickly to lock in the benefit. Alternatively the instrument could be stillborn: if the annex fails at WHA80 and the DG transition brings a leader who deprioritizes it, this may never happen and 76% by 2036 would be badly overconfident.

discrete_risks.name: Global interruption of wild poliovirus type 1 transmission
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: Zero wild poliovirus type 1 cases with onset in any 12 consecutive calendar months, per GPEI reporting, with the 12-month window closing inside the horizon.
discrete_risks.reasoning: 14 WPV1 cases in Afghanistan (11) and Pakistan (3) by July 2026 - the disease is confined to two countries but access, not epidemiology, is the binding constraint. Taliban restrictions on house-to-house campaigns, security in Pakistan's KP and Balochistan, vaccinator killings, and a global financing squeeze all cut against the GPEI 2027 target. The polio PHEIC was maintained at the 44th Emergency Committee on 4 March 2026.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: GPEI has missed eradication target dates in 2000, 2005, 2012, 2018 and 2023, and is on track to miss 2027 - five-plus consecutive misses. Its closest approach was 2021 (5 WPV1 cases globally), followed by rebound to 30 in 2022 and 99 in 2024. Conditional on 26 years at the last-two-countries stage, per-year interruption probability is low, roughly 5-7%.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: Type 2 and type 3 wild polio were both eradicated (2015, 2019) from similar-looking impossible endgames, and case counts genuinely are two orders of magnitude below 2014. A single successful negotiation with the Taliban on house-to-house access could flip this within 18 months. Conversely my numbers may be too high: cVDPV2 outbreaks in dozens of countries mean 'polio-free' is receding as a concept even if WPV1 stops, and donor exhaustion after another missed deadline could collapse the programme entirely.

discrete_risks.name: Laboratory accident causes an outbreak of 50+ confirmed human cases with official lab attribution
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: A national health authority, WHO, or an official government investigation publicly attributes an outbreak of at least 50 laboratory-confirmed human infections to a laboratory-acquired infection or a containment/biosafety breach.
discrete_risks.reasoning: BSL-3/4 capacity has expanded rapidly - over 60 BSL-4 labs operating or planned globally, many in countries with weak external oversight - while US governance moved in an unsettled direction: EO 14292 (5 May 2025) ordered replacement of the 2024 dual-use and nucleic acid synthesis frameworks, and as of July 2026 CRS could not determine whether replacement policies exist. Governance vacuum plus capacity growth raises accident probability; attribution remains the hard part.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: Laboratory escapes causing human outbreaks: Sverdlovsk anthrax 1979 (~66-105 deaths, attributed only in 1992), 1977 Russian flu H1N1 (large, never officially attributed), SARS-CoV escapes 2003-04 in Singapore, Taipei and Beijing (Beijing: 9 cases, 1 death), 2007 UK FMD (animal only). Events meeting both the 50-case and official-attribution bars: roughly 1 in 50 years, about 2%/yr, and attribution suppresses the observed rate well below the true rate.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: The resolution criterion is dominated by attribution politics, not biology. COVID-19 origins showed that even overwhelming institutional interest cannot produce official attribution, so the true underlying accident rate could be several times my figure while this question still resolves NO. Governments essentially never confirm their own labs caused an epidemic. Treat 11% by 2036 as a floor on reality and a ceiling on what gets acknowledged.

discrete_risks.name: Officially acknowledged incident where AI materially enabled acquisition or design of a dangerous pathogen or toxin
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: A national government, law enforcement agency, or frontier AI developer publicly confirms a specific incident in which AI systems materially assisted a person or group in designing, acquiring, or synthesizing a pathogen or toxin of biosecurity concern (beyond generic capability-evaluation results or red-team exercises).
discrete_risks.reasoning: Direction of travel is clear: in June 2026 Microsoft and multiple frontier developers publicly warned that AI protein-design tools can generate variants evading existing sequence-based DNA synthesis screening, and peer-reviewed 2026 work argues sequence screening plus KYC is no longer sufficient standalone. Congress has bills pending (House 2025, Senate January 2026) but no enacted mandatory screening statute, and the EO 14292-directed framework revision is unresolved. Capability is rising faster than the chokepoint is hardening.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: Zero confirmed incidents to date. Nearest reference class: serious non-state bioweapon acquisition attempts - Aum Shinrikyo (1990-95, failed), Rajneeshee (1984, succeeded with a low-grade agent), 2001 anthrax letters (insider access, not acquisition) - roughly one serious documented attempt per decade, with AI plausibly increasing attempt success rate rather than attempt frequency.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: The binding constraint on bioweapons has always been tacit laboratory skill and materials access, not information - Aum had PhD microbiologists, funding and facilities and still failed with anthrax. AI lowers the information barrier that was never the real barrier, so the real-world incident rate may barely move. Separately, developers and governments have strong incentives not to publicize such incidents, so this could resolve NO while the underlying phenomenon is common.

discrete_risks.name: Deliberate biological attack causes at least 10 confirmed human deaths
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: A government or international body attributes at least 10 human deaths to a deliberate release of a biological agent (state or non-state actor) in a single incident or campaign.
discrete_risks.reasoning: Barriers remain high but are eroding on several fronts at once: benchtop synthesizers diffusing outside screened supply chains, AI design assistance, published enhanced-pathogen methods, and weakened US and international oversight machinery. State programmes (Russia and North Korea assessed by SIPRI and US intelligence as maintaining capability) matter more than lone actors for the 10-death threshold.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: Deliberate biological attacks causing 10+ deaths in the past 80 years: essentially zero outside wartime (2001 anthrax letters: 5 deaths, 22 infections; Rajneeshee 1984: 751 ill, 0 deaths; Aum: 0 deaths from bio). Including accidental military releases (Sverdlovsk 1979, ~66 deaths) gives roughly 1 per 45 years, about 2%/yr as a generous ceiling; the pure deliberate-attack rate is well under 1%/yr.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: This is the archetypal risk expert communities have overestimated for 25 straight years - post-2001 forecasts of imminent mass-casualty bioterror were uniformly wrong, and the base rate has stubbornly refused to move despite two decades of biotech democratization, so 10% by 2036 may still be 2-3x too high. The opposite case: state use during an ongoing interstate conflict, particularly under a nuclear-shadowed stalemate, is the pathway most likely to break the historical pattern, and that pathway is more live in 2026 than at any point since 1990.

discrete_risks.name: Two consecutive years of rising global new HIV infections
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: UNAIDS reports annual new HIV infections higher than the preceding year in two consecutive reporting years, reversing the multi-decade decline.
discrete_risks.reasoning: International HIV financing fell 18% in one year to $7.3B (2025), the lowest in nearly two decades, and UNAIDS's July 2026 special report explicitly warns of reemergence. Lancet Global Health modelling suggests 0.77-2.93 million additional AIDS deaths by 2030 under sustained cuts. But 2025 data still showed the lowest infections and deaths in 30+ years, so the epidemiological turn has not yet appeared, and reporting lags mean the first plausible resolution is the 2028-2029 report cycle.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: Global new HIV infections have declined every year since the 1996 peak - 30 consecutive years - so the unconditional annual probability of even one year of increase is near zero. Conditional on an 18% one-year financing collapse plus PEPFAR disruption, this becomes a regime-change question rather than a base-rate question. Regional precedent: Eastern Europe and Central Asia have had rising incidence for two decades under funding withdrawal.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: Long-acting injectable PrEP (lenacapavir) is being scaled at generic prices through Global Fund and PEPFAR-adjacent channels precisely during this window, and it is the most effective prevention tool ever deployed - it could hold the line on incidence even with less money. Domestic financing substitution in South Africa, Nigeria, Kenya and Uganda has also been faster than modelled (the Lancet models explicitly assume zero substitution). Deaths may rise while incidence keeps falling, which would resolve this NO.

discrete_risks.name: United States formally rejoins the World Health Organization
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: The United States formally notifies WHO of resumption of membership, or deposits an instrument of acceptance of the WHO Constitution, and pays or commits to assessed contributions.
discrete_risks.reasoning: Withdrawal took effect January 2026 and the administration also rejected the 2024 IHR amendments (July 2025). No pathway exists before the January 2029 presidential transition; even then, rejoining requires paying arrears and would be politically costly. The 2021 precedent (rejoining on day one after the first withdrawal never took effect) shows it can be fast, but that reversal was legally simpler.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: US withdrawal-and-return from UN bodies: UNESCO (left 1984, returned 2003 - 19 years; left again 2017, returned 2023 - 6 years; announced departure again 2025); ILO (left 1977, returned 1980 - 3 years). Median return time roughly 6 years, heavily dependent on administration change. Conditional on a Democratic administration taking office January 2029, return probability within that term is high (~60-70%); unconditional probability requires weighting the 2028 election.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: Even a friendly future administration might not rejoin on the old terms - WHO's reform agenda, arrears of roughly $1.3B+, and durable congressional hostility could produce 'observer plus voluntary funding' instead of full membership, resolving this NO. Conversely, a fast reversal in early 2029 mirroring 2021 would make my 2031 figure too low; the distribution is bimodal around a single election, not smooth.

discrete_risks.name: WHO declares a global emergency over an antimicrobial-resistant pathogen
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: WHO declares a PHEIC, pandemic emergency, or equivalent formal global health emergency whose primary basis is an antimicrobial-resistant bacterial or fungal pathogen (for example pan-resistant Klebsiella, XDR typhoid, Candida auris, or drug-resistant gonorrhoea).
discrete_risks.reasoning: AMR kills more people annually than malaria and HIV combined (1.14M directly attributable in 2021, projected 1.91M by 2050) but is structurally a slow, distributed burden rather than a discrete detectable event - exactly the shape the IHR emergency machinery is bad at recognizing. Candida auris and XDR typhoid in Pakistan are the closest candidates, plus emerging artemisinin partial resistance in African malaria noted in the 2025 World Malaria Report.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: Zero AMR-based PHEICs in 17 years of the instrument, across 9 declarations - all were acute viral or vaccine-preventable events. The 2024 UN High-Level Meeting produced a political declaration, not an emergency framework.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: A genuinely pan-resistant, highly transmissible organism spreading through hospitals in multiple regions - the trajectory Candida auris has actually been on since 2016 - could force a declaration, and the amended IHR's broader pandemic emergency tier lowers the bar. If anything 8% by 2036 could be low if a hypervirulent carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella clone escapes healthcare settings into the community.

continuous_variables.name: Cumulative confirmed H5N1-infected US dairy herds
continuous_variables.notes: Verified 1,166 across 19 states at 22 Jul 2026 (Idaho 173). Growth decelerated from ~1,000/yr in 2024 to ~110-130/yr in 2025-26 as herd immunity and bulk-tank surveillance matured, but D1.1/D1.2 incursions add re-seeding risk. Monotone non-decreasing by construction - enforce a floor at the current value. Right-skewed: a new genotype adapting to cattle could add several hundred herds in one season.

continuous_variables.name: Confirmed human H5 (any NA) influenza cases reported globally per year
continuous_variables.notes: Verified: 12 cases Aug 2025-Jun 2026 globally; US total of 71 since 2024 has been nearly flat since early 2025. Extremely fat-tailed, better modelled lognormally with an added jump component: a single dairy or poultry season with poor worker protection produced ~65 US cases in 2024 alone. Floor at 0. The p90 here is NOT the pandemic scenario - that is the separate discrete node health_h5_sustained_human_transmission; condition the two so a transmission event forces this variable into the thousands.

continuous_variables.name: US confirmed measles cases per calendar year
continuous_variables.notes: 2026 verified at 2,295 through 22 Jul with the Feb-May peak past; full-year ~2,800-3,300. 2025 was ~2,200. Strongly right-skewed and highly autocorrelated within outbreak clusters but mean-reverting after a susceptible pocket is depleted - model as an overdispersed negative binomial with community-level depletion rather than a simple random walk. Drift should be driven by the kindergarten coverage variable.

continuous_variables.name: US kindergarten MMR vaccination coverage
continuous_variables.notes: Verified 92.5% for 2024-25 with exemptions at a record 3.6%; 92.7% and 3.3% for 2023-24. Herd immunity threshold is 95%. Decline has been steady and slow (~0.3-0.4pp/yr since 2019-20); the tail risk is a step change if federal de-recommendation survives litigation or several large states broaden non-medical exemptions, which justifies a regime-switching term rather than smooth drift. The national average masks large pocket variance; the outbreak-relevant quantity is the count of counties below 85%.

continuous_variables.name: Global DTP3 immunization coverage
continuous_variables.notes: Verified 85% for 2025 (WUENIC released 15 Jul 2026), still one point below 2019 and range-bound since 2009. Zero-dose children 13.5M. Downward drift reflects Gavi 6.0's ~$2.5B (21%) shortfall and the Global Fund's ~$7B gap beginning to bite from 2027, partially offset by strong domestic financing in middle-income countries. The series is unusually sticky - 16 years within a ~4-point band - so keep vol modest and treat any move beyond +/-3 points as a genuine structural break.

continuous_variables.name: Deaths directly attributable to bacterial AMR
continuous_variables.notes: Anchored on GRAM/Lancet (2024): 1.14M directly attributable in 2021, projected 1.91M by 2050 (~+0.022M/yr), with 4.71M associated. The current value is my interpolation to 2026, not a verified measurement. Genuinely smooth and predictable - the least volatile variable in the domain. Upside risk from artemisinin partial resistance in Africa and from reduced antibiotic access under health financing cuts; downside from improved WASH and vaccine-driven reductions in bacterial infection incidence.

continuous_variables.name: International financing for HIV in low- and middle-income countries
continuous_variables.notes: Verified: fell from $8.8B (2024) to $7.3B (2025), -18%, lowest in nearly two decades (UNAIDS, 27 Jul 2026). Drift assumes continued but decelerating withdrawal; the distribution is bimodal around the January 2029 US transition, so a two-regime model is more faithful than a single Gaussian. Floor around $2.5-3B representing Global Fund plus non-US bilateral commitments. Should drive the health_hiv_resurgence node with a 2-4 year lag.

continuous_variables.name: US adults currently using GLP-1 drugs for weight loss
continuous_variables.notes: Verified: 12.4% June 2026, up from 5.8% Feb 2024 (Gallup); 15% have ever tried; 91% awareness. Growth is decelerating and should be modelled logistically toward a ceiling of roughly 30-40% given ~85% two-year discontinuation among non-diabetics. Upside drivers: the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge demonstration (Jul 2026-Dec 2027), oral agents, and semaglutide patent expiry around 2031. Downside: payer retrenchment and the sizeable share who cycle off.

continuous_variables.name: US adult obesity prevalence (Gallup self-reported)
continuous_variables.notes: Verified: 36.4% in 2026 versus a 39.9% peak in 2022 - the first sustained multi-year decline in modern tracking, inversely tracking GLP-1 uptake. This is self-report (Gallup), which runs ~4-6 points below measured NHANES; use consistently and do not mix with NHANES levels. Drift should be made a function of the GLP-1 variable rather than exogenous. A payer pullback would flatten this within 2-3 years.

continuous_variables.name: WHO approved base programme budget per biennium
continuous_variables.notes: Verified: the 2026-27 budget was cut from $5.3B to $4.2B after US withdrawal (the US was ~18% of a ~$3.4B assessed base in 2024); roughly $1.7B remains unfunded even at the reduced level, i.e. WHO is short ~45% of its own reduced ask. Approved budget overstates realized spending. Upside from a 20% assessed-contribution increase and from Gulf/China/Germany substitution; a large upward jump if the US rejoins (see health_us_rejoins_who).

continuous_variables.name: Global malaria deaths
continuous_variables.notes: Verified 610,000 deaths and 282M cases in 2024 (World Malaria Report 2025, released 4 Dec 2025), up from 273M cases in 2023 - 94-95% in the African Region, 75% of those in under-fives. Upward drift reflects pyrethroid and artemisinin partial resistance plus Global Fund and PMI financing contraction, offset by R21/RTS,S rollout, which is the main reason drift is small rather than large. Reporting lags ~12 months, so simulation output should be dated accordingly.

continuous_variables.name: CDC full-time federal workforce
continuous_variables.notes: LOW CONFIDENCE - the roughly one-third reduction 'in just over a year' was verified via reporting, but I did not verify an exact current headcount; 9k is my inference from a pre-2025 base near 13k. Includes the compounding effect of the leadership vacuum (no Senate-confirmed director since Aug 2025; acting director and deputy both gone by Feb 2026) on voluntary attrition of senior scientists. Strongly bimodal on the 2029 transition. This is the best single proxy for US detection latency and should modulate the effective reporting delay on every US outbreak node.

feedback_loops.name: Coverage erosion to outbreak to polarization
feedback_loops.mechanism: Falling routine immunization creates susceptible pockets, which produce visible outbreaks (US measles at a 35-year high), which are absorbed into an existing political identity frame rather than changing behavior. Each outbreak strengthens both pro- and anti-vaccine mobilization, hardens exemption-seeking in already-low-coverage communities, and drives coverage there lower still. The national average moves slowly while cross-community variance widens, and it is the variance that drives outbreak counts.

feedback_loops.name: Outbreak to surveillance investment to detection
feedback_loops.mechanism: A salient outbreak mobilizes emergency funding, restores surveillance and testing capacity, and increases detection, which raises measured case counts and shortens time to containment. This stabilizer ended the 2014-16 and 2018-20 Ebola epidemics. It is currently the weakest it has been in twenty years: the WHO Ebola appeal is ~40% funded, WHO's own budget is cut a fifth with a further 45% unfunded, and CDC's workforce is down about a third - so the loop engages late and with less gain.

feedback_loops.name: Financing withdrawal to disease resurgence to higher future cost
feedback_loops.mechanism: Cuts to HIV, TB, malaria and immunization financing (international HIV funding -18% in one year; Gavi 21% short; Global Fund ~39% short) increase incidence and drug resistance with a 2-5 year lag. Higher incidence and resistance raise the per-case cost of control, so a constant or shrinking budget buys progressively less, forcing further triage. Donors then observe deteriorating outcomes, conclude the programmes are ineffective, and cut again.

feedback_loops.name: Panzootic scale to mammalian adaptation to spillover
feedback_loops.mechanism: Each additional infected mammalian host population - 1,166 US dairy herds, fur farms, marine mammals, domestic swine - provides more viral replication in mammalian cells, more selection for mammalian receptor binding and polymerase adaptation, and more human contact events. Adapted lineages then spread more easily to further mammal populations. Swine are the pivotal node because they support both avian and human receptor types and enable reassortment with seasonal influenza.

feedback_loops.name: Detection to trade and travel penalty to underreporting
feedback_loops.mechanism: Countries and producers that report novel pathogen detections face export bans, culling orders, travel restrictions and reputational cost, so the rational response is to test less and report later - US dairy herd testing was resisted for months in 2024 for exactly this reason. Reduced reporting lowers apparent global risk, which reduces political pressure to fund surveillance, which further reduces detection. The PABS deadlock is the international expression: countries will not share pathogen samples without guaranteed benefit-sharing.

feedback_loops.name: Institutional degradation to measurement collapse to false reassurance
feedback_loops.mechanism: When surveillance capacity falls, indicators improve spuriously - declining suspected Ebola cases in Ituri reflect testing breakdown rather than control, and flat US H5 human case counts partly reflect reduced worker testing. Decision-makers reading improving numbers cut resourcing further. This loop is especially dangerous because it inverts the sign of the system's own error-correction signal, and it is the largest source of bias in every indicator in this domain.

feedback_loops.name: Geopolitical fragmentation to weaker collective response
feedback_loops.mechanism: US withdrawal from WHO and rejection of the IHR amendments reduces both WHO's budget and its authority; other states then see less value in binding commitments (PABS deadlock, 11 IHR rejections), which weakens WHO further and slows collective response to the next event. Slower response produces a larger event, which produces nationalist border-closure responses rather than cooperative ones, eroding the multilateral instrument further.

feedback_loops.name: GLP-1 uptake to metabolic burden reduction
feedback_loops.mechanism: Rising GLP-1 use (5.8% to 12.4% of US adults in 28 months) is measurably reducing population obesity (39.9% to 36.4% on Gallup), which with a 5-15 year lag should lower diabetes, cardiovascular and some cancer incidence, easing healthcare system strain. Counterweights: ~85% two-year discontinuation among non-diabetics, cost barriers concentrating benefit among the insured and affluent, and the possibility that reduced obesity raises longevity and hence total lifetime healthcare consumption.

feedback_loops.name: Antibiotic access to survival to resistance
feedback_loops.mechanism: Expanding antibiotic access saves lives - GRAM estimates improved access and care could save 92 million lives 2025-2050 - but also increases selection pressure, raising resistance and future burden. The loop is genuinely two-signed: withholding access kills more people now than resistance kills later, so the balancing arm (stewardship) can only operate where access is already adequate, which is exactly where incremental resistance pressure is lowest.

structural_uncertainties: Measurement collapse can masquerade as improvement. Every headline indicator here is a detection-adjusted quantity, and detection capacity is falling sharply and unevenly - CDC workforce down roughly a third, WHO budget cut a fifth with 45% of the remainder unfunded, and Ebola suspected-case declines in Ituri that experts read as testing breakdown. A simulation calibrated on reported counts will systematically understate burden and, worse, will read weakening surveillance as declining risk. A serious version of this model needs an explicit latent-true-incidence layer with a time-varying, regime-dependent ascertainment fraction.

AI-bio capability could be a discontinuity, not a trend. The entire discrete-risk block for deliberate and accidental biological events is anchored on 20th-century base rates that assume tacit laboratory skill is the binding constraint. If frontier models plus automated cloud labs collapse that constraint - and June 2026 statements from Microsoft and other developers about screening evasion suggest movement in that direction - the natural-emergence base rate stops being informative and the tails of health_ai_enabled_bio_incident and health_bioterror_attack_10_deaths would need to be an order of magnitude fatter. Conversely, if information was never the barrier, these nodes are simply overpriced.

The January 2029 US transition makes several variables bimodal rather than diffusive. US WHO membership, PEPFAR levels, the federal immunization schedule, CDC capacity, and international HIV financing are governed largely by a single branch point rather than by continuous drift. Modelling them as Gaussian random walks produces a misleadingly smooth central mass and understates both tails. They should share a common latent regime variable resolved at the 2028 election.

Countermeasure discontinuity is under-weighted on the upside. A broadly protective influenza vaccine, a working pan-filovirus vaccine, long-acting injectable PrEP at true generic scale, or a phage or antivirulence breakthrough for gram-negative AMR would each break the assumed drift on multiple continuous variables at once. The model's structure is biased toward decline because degradation is currently more visible than innovation, but pharmaceutical step changes have repeatedly outrun forecaster expectations (lenacapavir, GLP-1s, R21).

Definitional and administrative capture of the key thresholds. 'Pandemic', 'PHEIC', 'elimination status' and 'attributable death' are administrative categories issued by institutions under political pressure, not physical facts. The amended IHR added a pandemic emergency tier that could inflate declaration rates; a weakened WHO facing member-state retaliation could deflate them; the US may simply decline to submit data that would trigger measles elimination revocation. Several discrete risks here could resolve opposite to physical reality.

Correlated compound shocks are not captured by treating this domain independently. The DRC Ebola epidemic is severe largely because of armed conflict, displacement and a simultaneous financing collapse - three domains interacting. Famine, mass displacement, conflict-driven vaccination interruption and health-financing withdrawal co-occur and multiply. Cross-domain coupling to the conflict, climate and macro modules will matter more for realized mortality than any within-domain parameter.

The reservoir may already contain the answer. My H5 estimates assume the observed 2025-26 deceleration in human cases is informative. It may instead reflect reduced testing of exposed workers, seasonal timing, or a lull before a genotype that has already acquired most necessary adaptations in swine. Serology in dairy and poultry workers has repeatedly found infections surveillance missed; the true human infection rate could be several-fold the confirmed count, changing both the adaptation opportunity and the effective CFR by a large factor in either direction.

A non-modelled pathogen class could dominate. This domain map is organized around the WHO priority list and current headline events. The historically most consequential emergences - HIV, COVID - were not on anyone's list. Fungal pathogens adapting to warming (the Candida auris pathway), vector range expansion under climate change (Oropouche, dengue in temperate zones), a prion-like agent, or chronic sequelae of a common infection could each generate burden comparable to anything explicitly modelled here, and none has a node.
